correctness.rationale: On a tree, unique paths make the uniformly seeded mean outbreak equal to 1+(2/n) times a sum of p to graph distance. Single-edge removal deletes exactly cross-cut pairs; the cross-cut reduction factors as 2p/n times an endpoint-distance generating-polynomial product. For every finite tree through order eight, the stand-alone code exhaustively enumerates Prüfer words, quotients by a complete center-rooted canonical invariant, checks polynomial coefficients by two independent methods, and finds exact all-nonnegative transformed coefficients yielding a universal optimizer for every class except two of the 23 eight-node types. The explicit two eight-vertex witnesses have all competitor polynomials dominated and exact score differences p(1-p-p²) and p(1-2p), giving genuine switches at the listed thresholds. An independent networkx tree-generation cross-check confirms exactly the same two canonical exceptional codes. This is exhaustive only for n≤8.

originality.rationale: This is a sharp smallest-order classification of the single-edge deletion minimizing expected final outbreak size from a uniformly random seed in independent bond percolation on trees. The previously published Moore–Newman percolation setup, Enns link-removal interventions, and Khorramzadeh parameter-dependent edge-reliability rankings do not state this complete finite-tree optimization result. The latter already exhibits a golden-ratio edge switch in a cyclic two-terminal network, so no novelty is claimed for switches generally or that number. Searching the research index, exact title/claim/parameter variants, did not find an implication of the present classification. Residual differently indexed or inaccessible exact precedents cannot be excluded.
residual_risks: Previously unindexed or privately circulated finite-tree link-intervention classifications may exist, including under susceptibility, mean reachability or reliability-polynomial terminology.
Only relevant sections, not every page or appendix, of some primary sources were materially read. An indirectly covering theorem in a full manuscript remains possible.
The current criterion is mean outbreak size with uniform seed; stronger or different stochastic epidemic models could invalidate its direct practical interpretation.

value.rationale: The exact natural first order at which preventive contact-edge selection must depend on transmissibility, together with all minimal topologies, exact transition values and a self-contained finite certificate, gives a structural benchmark for epidemic network intervention. It distinguishes the low-p locally influential cut from a high-p balancing cut. Unlike a mere numerical example or familiar general edge-ranking switch, it completely classifies the first possible failures of a uniform optimal intervention and settles the smaller orders. Importance is limited to this explicit mean-cluster percolation model, not claimed empirical generality.
